title: Promises made in a crisis
odia: ଆତଙ୍କ ବେଳେ ଯାଚନ୍ତି କୁକୁଡ଼ା, ଆତଙ୍କ ଗଲେ ଦିଅନ୍ତି ନେଫେଡ଼ା
literal_meaning: In a crisis they promise a chicken; once the crisis passes, they give a grin.
explanation: The saying contrasts an anxious promise with the grin offered once the danger has passed. Its source explains this as making a vow during trouble and then neglecting it. More broadly, it asks whether a promise still matters after the danger has passed.
meaning_odia: ବିପଦ ବେଳେ କୁକୁଡ଼ା ଦେବାକୁ ମାନସିକ କରନ୍ତି, କିନ୍ତୁ ବିପଦ ଟଳିଲେ ଖାଲି ଦାନ୍ତ ଦେଖାଇ ହସନ୍ତି—ଏହି ପାଠରେ ପ୍ରତିଶ୍ରୁତି ଓ ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ବ୍ୟବହାରର ଫରକ ଧରାପଡ଼େ। ସାହାଯ୍ୟର ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ସରିଗଲେ ବି ଦେଇଥିବା କଥାର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ରହିବା ଉଚିତ।
usage_example: After asking for urgent help and promising to return it, someone stops answering once their own problem is solved. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: ନେଫେଡ଼ା is read here as grinning or baring the teeth, a dictionary-attested sense that fits the contrast between promising and failing to deliver. The dictionary also records a wild-fruit sense; the present reading follows the vow-neglect context. The religious vow belongs to that setting, not to a claim about everyone’s practice.
